conventions.convention: Constraint classes are nonempty subsets C of a nonempty admissible truth class U. Restricted identifiability means injectivity of A restricted to C. Metrics need not respect vector operations; unspecified metrics default to discrete metrics.
The kernel-intersection criterion characterizes exact uniqueness only and asserts no stability bound.
Use real Stiefel frames with 1 ≤ p ≤ n and the induced Frobenius metric. The forward map is C¹ on an ambient open set containing all frames; the ambient gradient oracle is supplied.

The finite budget K may be zero; schedule indices begin at zero. A residual equal to the tolerance meets the target, an equal-objective trial is accepted, and the polar root is the positive-definite root. All operations are exact-arithmetic operations.

load_bearing.statement: An admissible constraint class is a nonempty subset C ⊆ U; its constrained forward map is A restricted to C. The class C is identifiable for A if that restriction is injective. C−C consists of differences of pairs in C.
Let X and Y be real vector spaces, let A:X→Y be linear, and let C⊆X be nonempty. The restriction A|C:C→Y is injective if and only if (C−C)∩ker A={0}.

For the supplied C¹ regularized objective, gradient oracle, initial Stiefel frame, tolerance, finite budget and positive schedule, test the initial residual; repeatedly project the gradient and form a polar trial; return on stationarity, objective increase or target attainment, and otherwise return the current frame when the budget is exhausted.

For the supplied C¹ objective and ambient gradient oracle, the projected vector is the Frobenius metric-dual gradient of the restricted objective, every polar trial is defined, and the procedure returns after at most K trial evaluations with a Stiefel frame. Accepted updates have nonincreasing objective, and target-met is returned exactly when the output residual is at most the tolerance.

seams_checked.note: The constrained-class definition specializes the nonempty admissible-truth and forward-map interface using explicit metrics. Its injectivity notion concerns exact truth recovery; neither the kernel criterion nor the examples infer stability.
The algorithm uses the real-Hilbert, open-domain forward-map interface and separately imposes C¹ regularity. It imports no tangential-cone hypothesis, identifiability result or convergence guarantee.
